description.narrative: The objectives of the Rebuilding Energy Infrastructure and Access Project for Haiti are to (a) strengthen the recipient's energy policy and planning capacity; (b) improve the sustainability and resilience of the recipient?s electricity sector and restore and expand access to reliable electricity services; and (c) provide financial assistance in case of an energy sector emergency. The project has three components. (1) Strengthening energy sector institutions and improving energy access. (2) Enhancing Electricite d'Haiti (EDH's) performance and rehabilitating and expanding infrastructure. (3) Energy sector risk and emergency response contingent reserve component will provide support upon occurrence of an energy sector emergency through: (a) the carrying out of emergency recovery and rehabilitation activities; and/or (b) technical assistance to support Ministry of Public Works, Transport, Energy and Communication (MTPTEC) and EDH in its response to an energy sector emergency.

The objectives of the Project are to (a) strengthen energy policy and planning capacity, (b) to improve the sustainability and resilience of the electricity sector and to restore and expand access to reliable electricity services, and (c) provide financial assistance to the electricity sector in case of an emergency.

title.narrative: People provided with new or improved electricity service

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Partially Achieved:  </strong>The revised target was achieved at 25 percent, reflecting the reduction of the project scope arising from implementation delays and cancelation and reallocation of resources.  The output is the number of radio frequency meters installed at new EDH customers after the rehabilitation of the 4 circuits (ADM 8-1, ADM 9-1., Mar 1-1, MAR 3-1.)</p>

<p><strong>Partially Achieved</strong>. The target for direct project beneficiaries was reached only at 76 percent of the revised target, because of the project’s support to the rehabilitation of the country’s distribution network, including the construction solar power plants with storage, and the expansion of solar electrification. Estimates of the number of direct beneficiaries include (i) 86,882 People benefiting from new or improved access to electricity, (ii) 19,040 Pupils benefiting from off-grid connecion, and (iii) 45,900 people benefiting from solar street lighting. Assuming that female represent 50 percent of beneficiaries, the target was also achieved at only 76 percent of the revised target.</p>
<p><strong>Partially Achieved:  </strong>The target of restored connections was achieved at 51 percent of the revised target, because of implementation shortcomings and cancelation of resources.</p>

<p><strong>Exceeded: </strong>The target was exceeded by 26 percent, reflecting the number of kilometers of distribution lines rehabilitated during the Rehabilitation of circuits ADM 8-1, ADM 9-1., Mar 1-1, MAR 3-1.</p>

<p><strong>Exceeded</strong>.  The target for off-grid connections were exceeded by 27 percent, as 19,040 students in rural and urban areas benefited from Photovoltaic Systems, including those installed in schools to supply interactive digital boards.</p>

title.narrative: Offgrid access to electricity for collective uses (street lighting, schools etc.)

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded</strong>:  640 Solar streetlights installed in the metropolitan area (Delmas, Nazon, Carrefour Feuille).  635 Solar streetlights installed in the North (Milot, Dondon, Route Cap Labadie). 358 Solar lights installed in the Champs de Mars squares (Port-au-Prince), and 405 Photovoltaic systems installed in Schools (in the 10 departments of Haiti).</p>

title.narrative: Capacity of Renewable Energy (including Hydropower) constructed or rehabilitated

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Partially Achieved. </strong>The following is the estimate of Installed Capacity: (i) Metropolitan area (Delmas, Nazon, Carrefour Feuille): 0.087 MW; North (Milot, Dondon, Labadie): 0.082 MW; Photovoltaic plant at Champ de Mars: 0.1 MW; Public schools:0.314 MW. Hydroelectricity rehabilitated: Drouet micro-hydroelectric plant undergoing rehabilitation: 2.5 MW. The Drouet rehabilitation is still underway because of COVID-19</p>

<p><strong>Exceeded</strong>: The revised target was exceeded following a rehabilitation of the distribution system and efforts by EDH to collect revenue from consumers.   The CRI achieved 37.80, or 8 percent above the revised target.</p>

<p><strong>Missed</strong>: The April 2021 situation for the metropolitan area and the provinces shows Technical losses: 18%, Non-technical losses: 52%. This is consistent with the fall in revenue collection observed since 2019.</p>
<p><strong>Achieved:</strong> The final report of the audit of the EDH accounts for 2006-2016 was available in February 2020</p>

actual.value: Carrying out the External Audit of EDH accounts over a period of 10 years. Final report received at the PCU in February 2020.

title.narrative: Strengthening of Government's oversight capacity and transparency in sector financial flows

baseline.value: Oversight capacity is weak in utility EDH, non existent in MTPTC Ministry.

target.value: Oversight capacity strengthened; Energy Cell with clear mandate and adequately staffed; Budgetary transfers to EDH and availabilityof financial outlook monitored.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Partially achieved</strong>: The Energy Cell and the ANARSE are operational, but they needed to be more effective in their operations, and the monitoring table for budget transfers to the electricity sector needs to be regularly updated.</p>

actual.value: The Energy Cell is fully operational. It is supporting implementation of the SREP and CTF projects. ANARSE is also operational. Capacity strengthening is continuing upon request. Monitoring of budgetary transfers to EDH are being posted regularly on the ANARSE's website

title.narrative: Government entity responsible for the energy sector adequately staffed

baseline.value: No Government entity exists to oversee the energy sector in Haiti

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Partially achieved:</strong> The target was achieved at 40 percent, with two permanent staff recruited against a target of 5. In the meantime, 5 technical experts and 3 administrative consultants were hired to support the energy cell.</p>

actual.value: 2 permanent staff allocated to support MTPTC's Energy Cell, composed with consultants funded under the project (5 technical expertsand 3 administrative consultants).

title.narrative: Electricity sector financial model and energy sector database

baseline.value: No model exists for the sector.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved: </strong>As part of the implementation of EDH's recovery plan and following the analysis of the existing model, an ad hoc financial projections tool, based on cash flows, up to 2030 has been developed. This model makes it possible to project the different EDH costs (operation, investments, financial cost) in different demand and supply scenarios, performance assumptions (technical and commercial losses, staff productivity) and financing plan (support for different types of investment by the State or by EDH).</p>

actual.value: The model is utilized to prepare budget proposal, inform the fiscal year, and simulate impact of commercial recovery actions on EDHfinancial sustainability. Model has been updated as part of the masterplan study, linking long term prospective with tariff structure.
